title: One Assistant, Many Memories: Benchmarking Real-World Group Assistance When Recall Is Not Enough
title_zh: 一位助手，多重记忆：当回忆不足时基准测试现实世界的群组协助

paragraphs.en: The value of memory lies not only in recall but in using it to provide appropriate assistance. Recent benchmarks test memory use in personalisation and agentic tasks, but seldom evaluate assistance without fixed answers or integration across multiple participants. Group chats make both challenges more acute: an assistant must integrate information from multiple members, track revisions and conflicts over time, and produce one response for the group. Yet existing group memory benchmarks rely on synthetic conversations and inherit constrained evaluation from general memory benchmarks, focusing on recall against fixed answers or decisions over a closed set. We introduce GroupAssistBench , the first memory benchmark from real-world group conversations with a deployed group assistant, covering 80,299 messages in 50 groups and costing over $53K. 1 1 1 See Appendix I for the cost breakdown. Over the same histories, GroupAssistBench evaluates memory recall (L1) with reference answers and memory use (L2) with service requests without fixed answers across single, distributed, and conflicting memories (M1–M3). Requests are verified to require group history, memories are anchored to their sources, and L2 uses tailored rubrics with penalties derived from real user feedback. Across evaluations of frontier models with full context, retrieval methods, and memory systems, the strongest memory system rivals full context on recall but falls far behind on use, especially for distributed and conflicting memories. Together, two additions that relate retrieved memories and bind remembered facts as response constraints bring consistent gains, showing that group memory systems must improve use, not recall alone.

paragraphs.en: Memory is a core component of agents built on LLMs and has been widely studied in recent years ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2025 ) . Recent benchmarks have moved beyond factual recall to evaluate whether remembered information supports personalization ( Jiang et al., 2025 ; Xiao et al., 2026 ; Xie et al., 2026 ) and agentic task completion ( He et al., 2026 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) . This shift from remembering information to using it effectively becomes especially challenging in multi-user settings. Group chats provide a particularly demanding setting for this shift from recall to use: unlike a personal assistant serving one user, an assistant in a group chat serves the group as a whole and must produce a single response that reconciles information distributed across members, revised over time, or contested within the group ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026b ; Owolabi, 2026 ; Ren et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 记忆是基于大语言模型构建的智能体的核心组成部分，近年来得到了广泛研究（Maharana 等，2024；Wu 等，2025；Hu 等，2025）。 近期的基准测试已超越事实性回忆，转向评估被记住的信息是否能支持个性化（Jiang 等，2025；Xiao 等，2026；Xie 等，2026）以及智能体任务的完成（He 等，2026；Zhao 等，2026）。 从记住信息到有效使用信息的这一转变，在多用户场景下尤其具有挑战性。 群聊为这种从回忆到使用的转变提供了一个要求尤为严苛的场景：与只服务单个用户的个人助理不同，群聊中的助理服务的是整个群体，必须生成单一回复，以协调分布在各成员之间、随时间被修订、或在群内存在争议的信息（Yang 等，2026；Hu 等，2026b；Owolabi，2026；Ren 等，2026）。

paragraphs.en: Existing benchmarks for group memory already examine how information is attributed, integrated, and updated, and show that systems designed for one user exhibit distinct failures in group settings ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Owolabi, 2026 ) . Yet their evaluation inherits a broader limitation of current memory benchmarks: success is measured primarily through recall. Questions ask who said what or which value is current and are scored against fixed reference answers, while tasks closer to assistance use multiple choice ( Hu et al., 2026b ) or selection from a closed set of actions ( Ren et al., 2026 ) . This leaves unanswered whether a system that retrieves the right memory can use it to respond appropriately to a service request without a fixed answer. Evidence from settings with one user shows why this distinction matters: on AlpsBench, memory raises persona awareness from 0.41 to 0.72 while reducing emotional appropriateness below the backbone without memory ( Xiao et al., 2026 ) . A separate limitation is that current benchmarks for group memory use synthetic conversations, leaving it unclear whether their tasks capture how agreements, corrections, and assistance failures arise in deployed groups ( Owolabi, 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026b ) .
paragraphs.zh: 现有的群体记忆基准已经在考察信息如何被归属、整合与更新，并表明为单用户设计的系统在群体场景中会出现明显的失败（Yang et al., 2026；Owolabi, 2026）。 然而它们的评估继承了当前记忆基准的一个更广泛的局限：成功主要通过回忆来衡量。 问题询问谁说了什么或哪个值是当前有效的，并对照固定的参考答案进行评分，而更接近辅助性质的任务则采用多选题（Hu et al., 2026b）或从封闭的动作集合中进行选择（Ren et al., 2026）。 这就留下了一个未解答的问题：一个检索到正确记忆的系统，能否在没有固定答案的情况下利用该记忆恰当地响应服务请求。 来自单用户场景的证据说明了这一区别为何重要：在 AlpsBench 上，记忆将角色意识从 0.41 提升到 0.72，同时使情感恰当性降到低于无记忆的主干模型（Xiao et al., 2026）。 另一个局限是，当前的群体记忆基准使用合成的对话，因此尚不清楚其任务是否能捕捉部署的群体中协议、纠正和辅助失败是如何产生的（Owolabi, 2026；Hu et al., 2026b）。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we introduce GroupAssistBench , a benchmark built on 50 group conversations involving a deployed assistant, containing 80K messages and 2,395 questions. GroupAssistBench organises evaluation along two orthogonal axes, include: 1) The task axis, aims to distinguish memory recall (L1), which asks a question about the history and has a reference answer, from memory use (L2), which poses a service request without a fixed answer and requires a reply that respects the memories it depends on. This axis measures whether a model can move from retrieving remembered information to using it appropriately in an open-ended response, and 2) The dependency axis, aims to distinguish whether the required memories are single (M1), distributed across members (M2), or conflicting (M3). This axis measures how well a model can integrate and reconcile memory evidence as its dependency structure becomes more complex. Figure 1 gives an overview of GroupAssistBench . Each request is verified to require the group history, and each required memory is anchored to a verbatim span in the original conversation. L1 answers are scored on atomic facts, while L2 replies are scored with rubrics tailored to each instance, whose penalty criteria are derived from real user feedback on the assistant. As shown in Table 1 , GroupAssistBench is the first benchmark that combines conversations among multiple participants with a deployed assistant, memory use through requests without fixed answers, and criteria derived from feedback.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate 14 configurations on GroupAssistBench , covering frontier LLMs with full context (e.g., Claude-sonnet-5 and GPT-5.6-terra), retrieval-augmented systems, and external memory systems. The results reveal a gap along each axis. Along the task axis, the strongest memory system surpasses Full Context with the same backbone on memory recall (0.621 vs. 0.570) but falls far behind on memory use (0.247 vs. 0.431). Along the dependency axis, the Full Context score for memory use drops from 0.505 on M1 to 0.303 on M3. Further analysis highlights two promising directions for group memory assistants: relational evidence organisation and assistance constraint binding (§ 5 ). Together, these results show that evaluating recall alone overstates the value of memory to a group. Our contributions are threefold:

sents.en: Further analysis highlights two promising directions for group memory assistants: relational evidence organisation and assistance constraint binding (§ 5 ).

sents.en: Together, these results show that evaluating recall alone overstates the value of memory to a group.
sents.zh: 总而言之，这些结果表明，仅凭召回评估会高估记忆对群体的价值。

sents.en: Our contributions are threefold:
sents.zh: 我们的贡献有三方面：

paragraphs.en: We introduce GroupAssistBench , the first benchmark built on real group conversations to evaluate memory along two axes: recall versus use, and single versus multiple or conflicting memories.
paragraphs.zh: 我们推出 GroupAssistBench，这是首个基于真实群组对话构建的基准，用于从两个维度评估记忆：回忆与使用，以及单一记忆与多条或冲突记忆。

paragraphs.en: We develop a traceable framework that verifies history dependence, grounds memories in source messages, and evaluates responses using criteria specific to each request and based on real user feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 我们开发了一个可追溯的框架，用于验证历史依赖性、将记忆锚定到源消息中，并使用针对每个请求且基于真实用户反馈的标准来评估回复。

paragraphs.en: Experiments across full context, retrieval methods, and memory systems reveal complementary retrieval and application bottlenecks that relational evidence organisation and assistance constraint binding mitigate.
paragraphs.zh: 在全上下文、检索方法与记忆系统上的实验揭示了互补的检索与应用瓶颈，而关系型证据组织与协助约束绑定可缓解这些瓶颈。

paragraphs.en: Long-term memory benchmarks began with factual recall over extended conversation histories ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2026c ) and have since turned to how memory supports downstream behavior, such as personalized responses ( Jiang et al., 2025 ; Xiao et al., 2026 ; Xie et al., 2026 ) , implicit constraints on later replies ( Li et al., 2026 ) , and multi-session agentic tasks ( He et al., 2026 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) . All of them target a single user and score memory use in a closed form, or judge free-form answers holistically ( Wu et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2026 ) , which does not tell which memory was used or misused. Rubric-based evaluation is finer grained ( Arora et al., 2025 ; Ding, 2026 ) , but its criteria are written by benchmark designers, and real user feedback has served only as a satisfaction label on the whole response ( Hong et al., 2026 ) . GroupAssistBench scores open-ended memory use whose required memories come from multiple users, with grounding criteria instantiated from the verified memories of each request and penalty criteria derived from real user feedback on the assistant’s failures, so that the criteria name which memory was misused.

paragraphs.en: GroupAssistBench evaluates whether a system can recall a group’s history and, more importantly, whether it can use that history to assist the group. This section formulates the tasks (Section 3.1 ), presents the construction pipeline that turns group conversations into instances (Section 3.2 ), and defines the scoring of responses (Section 3.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: GroupAssistBench 评估一个系统能否回忆起某个群组的历史，更重要的是，能否利用这些历史来辅助该群组。 本节对任务进行形式化（第 3.1 节），介绍将群组对话转化为实例的构建流程（第 3.2 节），并定义回复的评分方式（第 3.3 节）。

paragraphs.en: A group conversation is a chronologically ordered sequence H = ( m 1 , … , m T ) H=(m_{1},\dots,m_{T}) , where each message m t = ( u t , τ t , x t ) m_{t}=(u_{t},\tau_{t},x_{t}) consists of a speaker u t u_{t} , who is either a group member or the assistant, a timestamp τ t \tau_{t} , and a text x t x_{t} . A = { a 1 , … , a n } ⊂ H < c A=\{a_{1},\dots,a_{n}\}\subset H_{<c} is the set of required memories , the facts established in the history that a good response to q q depends on, each anchored to a message in H < c H_{<c} . K K is the answer key, a set of reference facts for memory recall or a rubric for memory use. Given H < c H_{<c} and q q , a system produces a response y ^ \hat{y} , and its goal is to score as high as possible under K K . paragraphs.en: Single memory (M1) instances depend on a single substantive memory. Multiple memories (M2) instances depend on multiple memories that must be combined, which in a group are typically contributed by different members. Conflicting memories (M3) instances have the structure of M2 and additionally contain a conflict pair ( a old , a new ) ⊂ A (a^{\mathrm{old}},a^{\mathrm{new}})\subset A : two values of the same matter, stated at different times or by different members, of which the conversation has made a new a^{\mathrm{new}} the current one. paragraphs.en: GroupAssistBench is built from Chinese group conversations in a deployed application, and the assistant replies are its original outputs. Messages are pseudonymized and rewritten to remove residual personal information, with English translations provided. The groups span everyday settings such as trip planning, classes, hobby communities, and project coordination. The evaluation set contains 2,395 instances sampled from 9.5K validated candidates across 50 groups and 80K messages. Although M2 is defined by the number of required memories, 56% of M2 and 93% of M3 instances draw anchors from at least two members. Table 2 reports the full statistics. Appendix A.1 details source selection, and Appendix G provides more examples.

paragraphs.en: The dependency type describes the structure of A A . Anchors from the same message and near-duplicate facts are merged into memory units; an instance is M1 if it depends on one unit and M2 if on two or more. M3 additionally requires a verified conflict pair ( a old , a new ) ⊂ A (a^{\mathrm{old}},a^{\mathrm{new}})\subset A . Candidate pairs are detected from update expressions and value changes in the history and matched to the anchor of the earlier value. Since two similar values may concern different matters, e.g., a lodging budget and a ticket price, each candidate receives three independent votes on whether the values concern the same matter, and only unanimously accepted pairs are used. Finally, we verify that a new a^{\mathrm{new}} is still current at the cutoff, and move the cutoff before the next change of the same matter if it is not.

paragraphs.en: Every instance passes deterministic gates: each anchor and cited premise must precede the cutoff, each span must be found verbatim in its message, and the query must neither reveal a required memory nor, for M3, hint that a value has changed. To assess the resulting quality, three annotators independently examined 120 instances stratified by level, dependency, and source: 95.8% are valid by majority vote and 84.2% unanimously, with pairwise agreement of 93–98% per question. On the 60 L2 instances, the annotators further rated each rubric for the soundness of its service criteria, the relevance of its penalty criteria, and its overall completeness; 90.0% of the rubrics pass all three checks by majority and 86.7% unanimously (Appendix C ).

paragraphs.en: Following prior work Zhao et al. (2026) ; He et al. (2026) , we compare three memory-access paradigms: Full Context , Retrieval-Augmented Systems , and External Memory Systems . We characterise their memory organisation using the topology taxonomy of Hu et al. (2025) : 1D flat memory has no explicit inter-unit relations, 2D planar memory organises units within a single structural layer, and 3D hierarchical memory connects representations across multiple abstraction levels. Full Context is a 1D reference that directly provides all prior messages and assistant trajectories, and we evaluate four backbones: Claude-sonnet-5, GPT-5.6-terra, Deepseek-v4-flash and Qwen-3.5-9b. Retrieval-Augmented Systems index the same history and include two 1D methods, BM25 and dense embedding retrieval, one 2D method, GraphRAG Edge et al. (2024) , and one 3D method, RAPTOR Sarthi et al. (2024) . External Memory Systems abstract, organise, or update the interaction history before retrieval. They include two representatives at each level: Mem0 Chhikara et al. (2025) and LightMem Fang et al. (2026) for 1D, A-MEM Xu et al. (2025) and MemoryOS Kang et al. (2025) for 2D, and xMemory Hu et al. (2026d) and EverMemOS Hu et al. (2026a) for 3D. This design covers both retrieval and external memory across the three topology levels without treating structural complexity as an ordering of capability.

paragraphs.en: Table 3 shows that Full Context methods remain competitive on both L1 and L2 tasks. DeepSeek-v4-flash obtains L1 met of 0.669 and L2 rubric score S ¯ \bar{S} of 0.469, while GPT-5.6-terra reaches 0.570 and 0.431, respectively. Within RAG systems, BM25 and dense retrieval obtain higher overall scores than GraphRAG and RAPTOR on both tasks, indicating that additional structural complexity does not consistently improve performance in this setting. Among external memory systems, hierarchical methods show promising L1 recall: EverMemOS and xMemory attain the met of 0.621 and 0.546, placing third and fifth among all evaluated baselines. Flat retrieval is more effective within RAG, whereas hierarchical systems show stronger L1 recall within external memory. This pattern is consistent with concerns that summary hierarchies can obscure factual distinctions Hu et al. (2026d) and highlights hierarchical memory organisation as an emerging direction for supporting reasoning across abstraction levels Hu et al. (2025) .

paragraphs.en: Performance generally degrades as queries move beyond dependence on a single memory. paragraphs.en: To examine whether reduced context usage during queries offsets memory construction, we compute total deployment cost over the full dataset as construction cost paid once plus retrieval and generation costs across all queries. Figure 3 separates these components. At the observed workload of all queries, BM25, dense retrieval, LightMem, RAPTOR, and Mem0 cost less than Full Context with the same GPT-5.6-terra task agent. For example, dense retrieval costs $55.0 in total, compared with $260.4 for Full Context, while RAPTOR reaches $204.5 after amortising its $127.6 construction cost. Lower cost, however, does not imply stronger performance. LightMem costs only $69.6 but obtains the lowest L1 and L2 averages, whereas EverMemOS achieves the highest L1 average among external memory systems but costs $814.9 and requires 11,138 queries to break even. Overall, an efficient memory system must balance construction overhead and savings with effective memory recall and assistance. Detailed statistics for each stage are reported in Appendix F.1 .

paragraphs.en: The gap between L1 and L2 does not show whether systems use memories they can recall, since the two levels contain different instances. We therefore identify 497 memories queried directly in L1 and required by an L2 request in the same group, and test whether each system uses in L2 what it recalls in L1 (Figure 4 ). Across all six memory systems, recalled but unused memories account for 21–27% of all pairs, versus 11–16% for models given full context. Even EverMemOS matches their recall (66% vs. 47–70%) but uses fewer recalled memories (65% vs. 73–85%). This fraction correlates more strongly with the L2 ranking in Table 3 ( ρ = 0.89 \rho=0.89 ) than recall itself does ( ρ = 0.56 \rho=0.56 ). Why are memories recalled at L1 left unused at L2? We split unused memories into those absent from the model input and those present but unapplied. (i) For memory systems, 36% of unused memories never entered the L2 input. This retrieval failure was cue dependent. L1 questions usually identify the target memory, whereas L2 requests often do not. Four of the six systems retrieved 84–100% of the same memories when L1 named them directly, and input coverage across all pairs rose from 62% to 83% as lexical overlap increased. (ii) The other 64% were in the input and still not used in the reply. This failure depends on the cue as well, with memories already in the input used more often when requests shared their wording or were framed around the same matter. Without such cues, memory systems can thus fail twice, in retrieving the relevant memory and in applying it when present. These failures motivate retrieving evidence independently of request wording and binding available memories to the response. Analyses by generation model and request type appear in Appendix F.2 .

paragraphs.en: The larger share of the loss comes from memories that reach the L2 input but remain unused. They account for 78% of unused memories for xMemory and 86% for EverMemOS. This application failure helps explain why EverMemOS falls from third on L1 to tenth on L2 and xMemory from fifth to thirteenth. We introduce Assistance Constraint Binding (ACB) , which determines each remembered fact’s subject, scope, status, and applicability, then binds the validated conditions to generation. paragraphs.en: We presented GroupAssistBench , a benchmark built from real-world group conversations with a deployed assistant. It evaluates memory recall and use over the same histories when the required memories are single, multiple, or conflicting. Required memories are anchored to source messages, and L2 rubrics translate real user feedback into criteria tailored to each request. Across LLMs given full context, retrieval methods, and memory systems, recall did not reliably translate into use. The strongest memory system surpassed the same backbone given full context on recall but lagged far behind on use, which declined further with multiple and conflicting memories. Relational Evidence Refinement and Assistance Constraint Binding improved all three tested memory systems by addressing complementary failures in retrieving relevant memories and applying those already available. We hope GroupAssistBench shifts memory evaluation from what systems recall to what they enable a group to do.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 GroupAssistBench，这是一个基于真实场景中部署助手的群聊对话构建的基准。 该基准在所需记忆为单条、多条或相互冲突的情形下，评估模型对相同历史记录的记忆召回与使用能力。 所需记忆锚定到源消息上，L2 评分标准将真实用户反馈转化为针对每次请求量身定制的判据。 在获得完整上下文的 LLM、检索方法和记忆系统中，记忆召回并不能可靠地转化为记忆使用。 最强的记忆系统在召回上超过了获得完整上下文的同一骨干模型，但在使用上远远落后，且在多条记忆和冲突记忆的情况下使用能力进一步下降。 关系证据精炼与协助约束绑定通过解决检索相关记忆和应用已有记忆这两方面互补的失败，提升了所有三个受测记忆系统的表现。 我们希望 GroupAssistBench 能将记忆评估从系统记住了什么，转向系统能让群体做成什么。

We also used generative AI tools to create or modify scientific figures and to summarise and analyse existing literature. Generative AI tools were not used to formulate mathematical claims. All AI-assisted outputs were reviewed by the authors. For example, research ideas suggested by LLMs were checked against the existing literature through a manual literature review to guard against unoriginal or unsupported claims, and LLM-generated code was manually reviewed, tested, and validated for correctness. We take full responsibility for the final content of this work, including all text, claims, code, figures, and other artefacts produced with the assistance of generative AI.

paragraphs.en: This study uses pseudonymized group-chat records. The use of these records for research was reviewed and approved through the data provider’s privacy review process before the data were made available to the authors. Speaker identifiers are replaced with group-specific aliases, and message texts are rewritten to remove residual personal information, with safety-filtered content explicitly marked. The original source records remain restricted to the data provider and will not be included in any public release. Any release of derived benchmark artefacts will undergo an additional privacy and compliance review to further reduce disclosure and re-identification risks.
paragraphs.zh: 本研究使用假名化处理的群聊记录。 在数据提供给作者之前，将这些记录用于研究的用途已通过数据提供方的隐私审查流程的审核与批准。 发言者标识符被替换为群组特定的别名，消息文本经过改写以清除残留的个人信息，经安全过滤的内容会被明确标注。 原始来源记录仅限数据提供方持有，不会包含在任何公开发布中。 任何派生基准测试产物的发布都将经过额外的隐私与合规审查，以进一步降低披露与重识别风险。

paragraphs.en: Upon acceptance, we will publicly release all author-owned code and privacy-reviewed derived benchmark artefacts necessary to reproduce the reported results. The benchmark release will include the rewritten and pseudonymized Chinese and English group histories, member profiles, queries, per-instance history cutoffs and split manifests, source-linked anchors and evidence spans, L1 reference and distractor atoms, and L2 rubrics with criterion types and weights. The code release will include the exact task and evaluator prompts, benchmark construction and validation pipeline, evaluator parsing and deterministic scoring code, result aggregation scripts, author-written baseline adapters, configurations, the relational evidence organisation and assistance constraint binding implementations, end-to-end run scripts, dependency specifications, and model and API version information. We will also release the model responses, evaluator judgments, and aggregate run metadata underlying the reported tables so that the reported scores can be verified without rerunning proprietary models. For third-party implementations or model weights that we cannot redistribute, we will provide versioned references together with our patches, adapters, and configurations. All released artefacts will be accompanied by explicit licenses or data-use terms. Original source records and the other restricted materials listed in the Ethics Statement will remain private.
paragraphs.zh: 论文录用后，我们将公开发布全部作者自有代码以及经隐私审查的、复现所报告结果所必需的衍生基准工件。 基准发布内容包括：改写并去标识化的中英文群聊历史、成员档案、查询、逐实例的历史截断点与划分清单、带来源链接的锚点与证据片段、L1 参考原子与干扰原子，以及带有评分标准类型和权重的 L2 评分细则。 代码发布内容包括：精确的任务与评估器提示词、基准构建与验证流水线、评估器解析与确定性打分代码、结果汇总脚本、作者编写的基线适配器、配置文件、关系型证据组织与协助约束绑定的实现、端到端运行脚本、依赖规格说明，以及模型与 API 版本信息。 我们还将发布支撑所报告表格的模型响应、评估器判定和汇总运行元数据，以便无需重新运行专有模型即可验证所报告的分数。 对于无法再分发的第三方实现或模型权重，我们将提供版本化引用，并附上我们的补丁、适配器和配置。 所有发布的工件都将附带明确的许可证或数据使用条款。 原始来源记录以及伦理声明中列出的其他受限材料将保持不公开。

sents.en: We will also release the model responses, evaluator judgments, and aggregate run metadata underlying the reported tables so that the reported scores can be verified without rerunning proprietary models.

paragraphs.en: All conversations are de-identified before they reach the authors. Member identifiers are replaced with per-group pseudonyms, message texts are rewritten to remove residual personal information while preserving the facts, values, and speaker of each message, and a small fraction of messages (2.5%) are replaced by placeholders of a safety filter. Non-text messages such as images and files are kept as placeholders that name the attachment. paragraphs.en: A service point is a message that mentions the assistant or immediately precedes an assistant reply. A lightweight classifier discards service points that are not requests, such as small talk or comments on a previous reply. Each remaining request is answered twice by the same model, once with the preceding history and once without it, and a comparator labels the contribution of the history as strong , weak , or none . Requests labelled none are discarded. Information that only appears in earlier assistant replies is excluded when judging the contribution, since it is generated content rather than memory of the group. Of 13,782 service points, 10,191 are requests and 7,926 are retained (6,772 strong and 1,154 weak).
paragraphs.zh: 服务点是一条提及助手或紧跟在助手回复之前的消息。 一个轻量级分类器会丢弃那些不是请求的服务点，例如闲聊或对之前回复的评论。 每个剩余的请求由同一个模型回答两次，一次带有前置历史，一次不带前置历史，由一个比较器将历史的贡献标注为强、弱或无。 被标注为「无」的请求会被丢弃。 仅出现在较早助手回复中的信息在判断贡献时会被排除，因为它是生成的内容而非对群的记忆。 在 13,782 个服务点中，10,191 个是请求，7,926 个被保留（6,772 个为强，1,154 个为弱）。

paragraphs.en: Anchors are proposed in one call with two passes. The first pass extracts candidate facts that the response depends on, and the second pass removes candidates whose absence would not change the response. Each anchor must state its fact without pointer expressions such as “the time mentioned above”, and anchors that contain such expressions are rejected by a word list. The evidence span of each anchor is matched verbatim against the cited message, and anchors that fail are rejected (154 of 22,843 proposals). When a fact appears repeatedly, a rescan of the history anchors it to the earliest message that establishes it, and earlier lexical matches are flagged since a lexical match does not necessarily establish the same fact. Anchors whose source message is an assistant message are marked, and the reviewer in Appendix A.6 checks whether they relay a fact established by a member. Verified anchors are tracked in a per-group inventory that records which instances consume each anchor, which is used to select uncovered anchors for authored instances.
paragraphs.zh: 锚点通过两次处理在单次调用中提出。 第一次处理提取回复所依赖的候选事实，第二次处理则移除缺失后不会改变回复的候选事实。 每个锚点必须直接陈述其事实，不得使用诸如「上文提到的时间」之类的指代表达，包含此类表达式的锚点会被词表拒绝。 每个锚点的证据片段会与被引用的消息逐字匹配，匹配失败的锚点将被拒绝（22,843 个提议中有 154 个）。 当同一事实重复出现时，对历史记录的重新扫描会将其锚定到最早确立该事实的消息，而更早的词汇匹配会被标记，因为词汇匹配不一定确立相同的事实。 来源消息为智能体消息的锚点会被标记，附录 A.6 中的审阅者会检查它们是否转述了由成员确立的事实。 已验证的锚点会记录在按群组维护的清单中，记录哪些实例消费了每个锚点，该清单用于为撰写实例选择未被覆盖的锚点。

paragraphs.en: Candidate conflict pairs are detected from update expressions and from changes of the value in the same slot, and each new value is paired with the anchor that established the earlier value. Disagreements between members are included only if the conversation later resolves them. Each candidate pair receives three independent votes on the relation between the two values, including true update , different slot , range extension , rephrase , and goal versus status . Pairs with three true update votes are accepted, and the other pairs are not used unless a human annotator confirms them. Of 595 candidate pairs, 338 are accepted. For each accepted pair, we check that the new value is still current at the cutoff. If the matter changes again later, the cutoff is moved before the next change, or the pair is dropped. A M3 instance further requires at least two anchors on the same matter from members other than the one who makes the update, so that it keeps the structure of M2. The superseded value is excluded from the grounding criteria and enters the penalty criteria instead (Appendix B ).

paragraphs.en: Native instances keep the original request of a member and place the cutoff at the request message. For authored instances, the query type is assigned by the pipeline in rotation from a list of nine types: single-fact recall, multi-entity attribute mapping, attribution, state tracking, constraint compliance, update resolution, aggregation, personalized assistance, and arbitration among members. Every factual premise in an authored query must cite a source message and a matching span, which is verified in the same way as an anchor. The cutoff of an authored instance is placed between δ min = \delta_{\min}= 20 and δ max = \delta_{\max}= 200 messages after its last anchor (Section 3.2 ), so that the instances cover a range of distances between a memory and its use, and no update of the same matter may fall within this range. How the cutoff restricts the input of each system at evaluation time is described in Appendix E.1 . For L1 instances, the reference answer is split into atomic facts, one for each anchor, and for M3 instances the superseded value is recorded as a distractor. Rubrics of L2 instances are assembled as described in Section 3.3 and Appendix B .

sents.en: The cutoff of an authored instance is placed between δ min = \delta_{\min}= 20 and δ max = \delta_{\max}= 200 messages after its last anchor (Section 3.2 ), so that the instances cover a range of distances between a memory and its use, and no update of the same matter may fall within this range.

paragraphs.en: An instance is rejected if (i) any anchor or cited premise does not precede the cutoff, (ii) any evidence span is not found verbatim in the cited message, (iii) the query reveals a required memory, names an evaluation dimension, or, for M3 instances, contains words that hint at a change, (iv) the cutoff leaves almost no history, or (v) the rubric violates the constraints in Appendix B .
paragraphs.zh: 若出现以下情况，则该实例将被拒绝：(i) 任何锚点或引用的前提不位于截断点之前；(ii) 任何证据片段无法在引用的消息中逐字找到；(iii) 查询泄露了所需记忆、点明了评估维度，或对于 M3 实例而言，包含暗示某种变化的词语；(iv) 截断点之后几乎不保留历史记录；或 (v) 评分规则违反附录 B 中的约束条件。

paragraphs.en: A reviewer model then checks (i) whether each anchor is necessary, by testing whether a smaller set of anchors is sufficient, (ii) whether the query can be answered from its own wording, (iii) whether an anchor in an assistant message relays a fact established by a member or content generated by the assistant, and (iv) whether the two values of a M3 instance belong to the same matter. For every negative judgment the reviewer must quote the span that supports it, and quotes that are not found in the conversation invalidate the judgment. paragraphs.en: We validated three things by hand: the instances themselves, the rubrics of the L2 instances, and the criterion-level judgments of the automatic judge. All three studies use the same sample of 120 instances drawn from the evaluation set, stratified by task level, memory dependency, and source (10 per cell), excluding instances that the pipeline had marked as superseded, and the same three annotators: one author and two annotators from the data provider, all fluent in Chinese and familiar with the group-chat setting. Annotators worked independently and did not see the outputs of the gates, the model reviewer, or the judge. An earlier annotation of the same sample by a second author was excluded: a joint review found that it had applied a stricter reading of the guidelines than the guidelines intended (it rejected 24% of the instances, against 5–10% for the three annotators, and agreed with them on only 71–79% of the instances), and the guidelines were clarified before the annotation reported here. We report raw agreement rather than a chance-corrected coefficient: valid judgments dominate every annotator’s marginals, so coefficients such as Cohen’s κ \kappa have almost no room above chance and are uninformative here.

paragraphs.en: By majority vote, 95.8% of the instances are valid (93.3% L1, 98.3% L2; 95.0/92.5/100% for M1/M2/M3), and every question is accepted by at least 97.5% by majority. Agreement is uniform across the three pairs (90–93% on the instance level, 93–98% per question), with no annotator systematically stricter than the others: of the 480 judgments, 464 are unanimous, 15 are rejected by a single annotator, and one is rejected by two. paragraphs.en: The instance-level check asks whether a rubric is valid as a whole. paragraphs.en: The judge agrees with the human majority on 89.3% of the judgments, the same level as the annotators agree with one another (mean pairwise 0.898, range 0.88–0.93), and it agrees with the strictest annotator (0.915) more often than that annotator agrees with the other two. On grounding and service criteria the judge only misses: it never credits a grounding criterion the majority rejects, but fails to credit 14.2% of the grounding criteria and about 11% of the service criteria that the majority accepts, typically when the response states the fact in paraphrase rather than in the wording of the rubric. On penalty criteria it only over-penalizes: it never overlooks an error the majority found, but flags 4.7% of the penalty criteria that the majority considers not violated. Both directions lower the scores; neither raises them. At the instance level, recomputing score and pass from the human judgments with the formula of Section 3.3 gives a pass agreement of 88.9% and a score correlation of r = 0.84 r=0.84 ( ρ = 0.84 \rho=0.84 ) with the judge, above the mean between annotators (86.3% and r = 0.81 r=0.81 ); the judge’s mean score is 0.13 below the human majority, and the ranking of the three systems is identical under the judge and under every annotator. Responses that decline to answer (25 of the 60 EverMemOS responses) are not a source of disagreement: on these the judge and the majority agree on 95–100% of the criteria. paragraphs.en: GroupAssistBench comprises 2,395 questions grounded in conversations from 50 groups: 1,374 questions for memory recovery (L1) and 1,021 for memory use (L2). Each question is assigned to one of three memory dependency levels. M1 ( Single ) requires one substantive memory, M2 ( Integrative ) combines complementary memories, and M3 ( Evolving ) resolves updates, conflicts, or differences in applicability. The corpus contains 80,299 message records and 4,924,259 tokens. Table 10 summarizes the question distribution and variation across groups. Group histories range from 2,887 to 972,839 tokens, with ten groups exceeding 100,000 tokens and four exceeding 200,000 tokens.

paragraphs.en: The accounting reveals two distinct efficiency regimes. BM25, dense retrieval, LightMem, and RAPTOR recover their construction costs within the dataset, but their low costs do not yield the strongest task scores. Conversely, several structured memory systems improve L1 recovery while requiring more queries to recover their construction costs. Overall memory efficiency should therefore consider evidence utility and service quality together with construction costs and expenditure during queries, rather than equating shorter context with a better memory system.
paragraphs.zh: 该核算揭示了两种截然不同的效率模式。 BM25、稠密检索、LightMem 和 RAPTOR 能在数据集内收回其构建成本，但它们的低成本并未带来最强的任务得分。 相反，一些结构化记忆系统在提升 L1 回收的同时，需要更多查询才能收回其构建成本。 因此，整体记忆效率应当把证据效用和服务质量与构建成本以及查询期间的开销放在一起考量，而不是把更短的上下文等同于更好的记忆系统。

paragraphs.en: L2 requests are either written by group members (native) or authored by the pipeline; authored requests are checked not to reveal the memory, but they ask about the matter the memory bears on, whereas native requests are ordinary messages. The two types have almost the same distribution of lexical overlap with the memory (30%/49%/21% vs. 35%/48%/17% of memories at zero, low and higher overlap), and memories enter the input equally often (69% vs. 67% for memory systems). Yet memories in the input are used less often on native requests: 58% vs. 71% for full context, 38% vs. 61% for retrieval, and 30% vs. 51% for memory systems, and the gap persists within each overlap band (e.g., at zero overlap 56% vs. 65%, 32% vs. 52%, 19% vs. 41%). The cue that drives memory use is therefore not shared wording but whether the request is framed around the matter at all; questions in existing memory benchmarks are, and requests in real group chats are not.
paragraphs.zh: L2请求要么由群组成员撰写（原生请求），要么由流程生成；系统会检查生成的请求不会泄露记忆内容，但这些请求会询问记忆所涉及的事宜，而原生请求则是普通消息。 两种类型与记忆的词汇重合度分布几乎相同（在零重合、低重合和较高重合的记忆中分别为30%/49%/21%与35%/48%/17%），且记忆进入输入的频率也基本相同（记忆系统为69%与67%）。 然而，输入中的记忆在原生请求上被使用的频率更低：完整上下文为58%对71%，检索为38%对61%，记忆系统为30%对51%，且这一差距在每个重合度区间内都持续存在（例如，在零重合时分别为56%对65%、32%对52%、19%对41%）。 因此，驱动记忆使用的线索并非共同的措辞，而是请求是否围绕该事宜本身展开；现有记忆基准中的问题是围绕事宜的，而真实群聊中的请求则不是。

paragraphs.en: RER operates between retrieval and answer generation. Given a query and its retrieved evidence, it identifies items that concern the same members, events, or decisions, organises them to expose complementarity, chronology, updates, and conflicts, and adds missing supporting items from the eligible candidate pool when necessary. It preserves the original history cutoff and source identifiers.
paragraphs.zh: RER 在检索与答案生成之间运行。 给定一个查询及其检索到的证据，它会识别涉及相同成员、事件或决策的条目，对它们进行组织以呈现互补性、时间顺序、更新与冲突，并在必要时从符合条件的候选池中补充缺失的支撑条目。 它保留原始的历史截止点和来源标识符。

paragraphs.en: ACB interprets retrieved memories as constraints on the current assistance response. For each constraint, it records the affected subject, scope, content, status, applicability, source identifiers, and an exact supporting quotation. Code verifies the source and quotation, removes duplicate or inapplicable constraints, and supplies the validated constraint block as a separate input to answer generation. Thus, ACB changes how retrieved evidence governs the response without adding new memories.
paragraphs.zh: ACB 将检索到的记忆解释为对当前辅助响应的约束。 对于每个约束，它记录受影响的主体、范围、内容、状态、适用性、来源标识符以及一段精确的支持引文。 代码验证来源和引文，移除重复或不适用的约束，并将经过验证的约束块作为独立输入提供给答案生成。 因此，ACB 改变了检索到的证据管理响应的方式，而无需添加新的记忆。

paragraphs.en: This section documents the task and evaluation protocol used for the reported experiments. We evaluate each method end to end using its official implementation where available, together with its method-specific memory construction and retrieval procedures. All retrieval and external memory systems use GPT-5.6-terra as the task agent, and all reported outputs are scored by GPT-5.6-sol with the same task-level criteria and scalar scoring rules. Method-specific context wrappers and response formats are retained where required by the corresponding implementations; these differences are treated as part of each complete system rather than as changes to benchmark questions or scoring.

paragraphs.en: The human-labor subtotal reports compensation actually paid to contributors. It covers benchmark and protocol design; construction and review of seed cases, queries, anchors, ground truths, and rubrics; M3 update and conflict annotation; L1–L2 pair verification; quality review and adjudication; and baseline adaptation, reruns, result verification, and statistical analysis. Converting paid workdays to eight-hour days, benchmark design involved two experts for approximately 15 days each (240 person-hours), dataset construction involved four experts for approximately 15 days each (480 person-hours), and quality assurance and validation involved ten experts for approximately two days each (160 person-hours). Automated model execution is excluded from person-hours; only active construction, review, debugging, monitoring, and validation time is counted.
